findings.title: Substantive technical definitions are marked source-verified without a supporting definition authority
findings.evidence: The cited syllabus rows name these terms or list them as required vocabulary/methods, but do not define validation as rule-based acceptance that cannot prove correctness, double entry as independent entry twice for comparison, entity as a distinguishable subject, or the identifying/reference semantics assigned to the database keys. The rows nevertheless use en_status=SOURCE_BOUNDARY_VERIFIED and cite only the syllabus. The source_ref claim_scope says term occurrence and syllabus boundary, which does not support the added definition content.
findings.impact: Downstream glossary v2 or lesson authors could treat an analyst-authored technical definition as syllabus-verified authority, violating provenance and the work-order rule for unsupported definitions.
findings.required_fix: Audit every non-command technical row. For each substantive definition beyond explicit syllabus wording, either add a permitted reviewed technical authority with an exact locator and claim scope, or reduce the text to occurrence/scope boundary and set an English status that clearly remains a technical candidate pending review. Preserve the accepted syllabus classifications for check digit, verification and the two-table DML limit.
findings.required_retest: Issue glossary-v1 correction as a new artifact version with new hashes. A fresh independent A3 reviewer must rehash inputs/outputs, verify every affected definition against its exact authority, and repeat the 96-row/123-reference/status checks. A4 must independently recheck command-language boundaries if any shared row changes.
